errors.claim: Finance is positioned as a decision-making toolkit, not a body of doctrine.
errors.searches: "decision makers"; "body of doctrine"; doctrine; "Finance is also a tool"
errors.source_check: The source calls finance a tool for better decision-making and says business finance develops tools for repeatable decisions. It does not contrast finance with a "body of doctrine"; that negative framing is added synthesis.

errors.claim: Limited partners may have unlimited liability for designated general partners only.
errors.searches: limited partners; designated partners; unlimited liability; general partner; LLP
errors.source_check: The source says only designated partners have unlimited liability; other partners may be designated limited partners and are liable only up to their initial contribution. The reference reverses who bears unlimited liability.

errors.claim: FRED is a primary source for empirical work in finance.
errors.searches: FRED; "765,000"; "primary source"; "empirical work"; "largest sources of economic data"
errors.source_check: The source calls FRED one of the largest sources of economic data, describes its contents, and notes that data can be downloaded for analysis. It does not call FRED a primary source for empirical finance work.

errors.claim: The August 2018-2020 yield-curve inversion preceded the COVID recession.
errors.source_check: The recession-signalling substance is supported, but the date range is not: the source says the curve was normal in August 2018, inverted in March 2019, and remained inverted into 2020.

errors.claim: US firms had a combined market capitalisation of $50.8 trillion at the end of 2020, about 66 per cent of the world total estimated at $90 trillion.
errors.source_check: The source says $50.8 trillion was over half of the approximately $90 trillion world total. Its separate 66% figure is the S&P 500 firms' share of the $50.8 trillion US market, not the US share of world capitalisation.

errors.claim: Bill Gross was the founder of Pimco.
errors.searches: "Profile of Bill Gross"; founder; cofounder; cofounded; Pimco
errors.source_check: The source says Gross cofounded Pimco in 1971. Calling him its founder drops the cofounder qualification.

errors.claim: The Janet Yellen, Bill Gross, and Warren Buffett profiles are all framed as illustrating long-term investing discipline.
errors.searches: "Profile of Janet Yellen"; "Profile of Bill Gross"; "Warren Buffett"; "long-term investing"; discipline
errors.source_check: Buffett is explicitly associated with long-term investing, but Yellen's profile is framed around career firsts and public economic service, while Gross's concerns fixed-income strategy and efficient markets. The source supplies no common long-term-investing frame for all three.

errors.claim: US average annual real GDP growth at the start of the millennium was $10 trillion in 2000 to over $21 trillion in 2020.
errors.searches: "$10 trillion"; "$21 trillion"; "Historical Trends in GDP"; nominal GDP; real GDP; average annual growth
errors.source_check: The source gives approximately $10 trillion and over $21 trillion as annual GDP levels in current dollars and then identifies such current-price measurement as nominal GDP. These are neither an average annual growth measure nor real-GDP values.

errors.claim: The default recommendation for a diversified portfolio is approximately 12 stocks.
errors.searches: Statman; "dozen stocks"; "exact number"; "reasonably diversified portfolio"; default recommendation
errors.source_check: The source explicitly says there is no exact number on which financial managers agree, then says an average investor can create a reasonably diversified portfolio with approximately a dozen stocks. Calling this a default recommendation overstates the qualification.

errors.claim: A 30-year fixed mortgage on $140,000 at 3.6% produces over $56,000 in total interest.
errors.source_check: The source example finances $140,000 over 20 years at 3.6%, producing $56,597.02 in interest. The reference changes the term to 30 years while retaining the 20-year interest result.

errors.claim: Adam Smith and Karl Marx are referenced as classical political economists.
errors.searches: "Adam Smith"; "Karl Marx"; "early political economists"; "classical political economists"; factors of production
errors.source_check: The source calls them "Early political economists" and supports the associated factors-of-production claim. It does not apply the added classification "classical".

errors.claim: Janet Yellen's tenure saw 12 months of consecutive employment increases, a Federal Reserve historical first.
errors.searches: "12 months" employment; "every month of her term"; "four-year tenure"; "continuous increases"; Janet Yellen
errors.source_check: The source says employment increased in every month of Yellen's four-year term and calls that entire-tenure record the first and only such occurrence. It does not say 12 months.

errors.claim: Payday advance loans and refund anticipation loans are products on which borrowers speculate.
errors.searches: payday advance loan; refund anticipation loan; speculate; speculating; borrower; short-term loan; 364%
errors.source_check: The source describes PALs and RALs as short-term borrowing arrangements and strongly criticises their effective costs. It does not characterise using them as speculation; that term misstates the transaction while the accompanying cost warning remains faithful.
